top_stories.title: Ukraine Legalizes and Taxes Its Crypto Market
points: Ukraine passed legislation legalizing cryptocurrency, effective from July 2027, providing regulatory clarity for the country's crypto ecosystem.
The law imposes an 18% tax on crypto profits plus a 5% military levy on gains, with stablecoins (cryptocurrencies pegged to a stable asset like the U.S. dollar) placed under central bank oversight.

unique_angles.point: Frames the move as positioning Ukraine as crypto-friendly, potentially encouraging institutional adoption and crypto-based economic activity.
Details the specific tax structure (18% profit tax plus 5% military levy) and central bank oversight of stablecoins.

items.title: Bitcoin's Sharp Decline Amid Macro Pressures
points: Bitcoin fell below $58,000 (dipping as low as $57,500) Wednesday amid strong U.S. GDP growth (revised up to 4.3%), PCE inflation (the Fed's preferred inflation gauge) matching a 3-year high of 3.8%, and proposed Trump tariffs on 14 economies.
Bitcoin has since recovered to around $59,600 but remains down 5% for the week, as stronger economic data raised expectations for a December Fed rate hike, pressuring risk assets.

items.title: HYPE Leads Altcoin Losses After Trader Exit
points: HYPE, the native token of derivatives exchange Hyperliquid, fell nearly 10% over the past week—the steepest drop among the top 10 cryptocurrencies.
The decline followed Abraxas Capital, one of Hyperliquid's most profitable traders, shutting down its operations on the platform, raising concerns about the exchange's outlook.

items.title: Bitcoin ETFs See Record Monthly Outflows
points: U.S. spot Bitcoin ETFs (funds that track Bitcoin's price) saw $4.94 billion in net outflows in November, their worst month on record.
This marks a sharp reversal from prior months of inflows, signaling weakening institutional and retail demand amid macro headwinds.

items.title: France Rejects Self-Custody Wallet Declaration Rule
points: France's Senate rejected a proposal requiring holders of self-custody wallets (digital wallets held directly by the owner, not an exchange) worth over €100,000 to declare them.
Lawmakers cited security risks, including kidnappings targeting crypto owners in the country, as the reason for rejection.

items.title: Saylor's Strategy Plans to Buy All Remaining Mineable Bitcoin
points: Michael Saylor's company Strategy says it plans to acquire roughly 900,000 bitcoin still left to be mined before the 21 million supply cap is reached.
If executed, this aggressive accumulation strategy would position Strategy as one of the largest bitcoin holders, consolidating a major share of future supply.

sections.title: Bitcoin's Sharp Decline and Market Pressures
points: Bitcoin dipped as low as $57,500 on Wednesday amid a confluence of negative macro signals: third-quarter U.S. GDP revised up to 4.3%, PCE inflation (the Federal Reserve's preferred measure) matching a 3-year high of 3.8%, and the Trump administration proposing tariffs on 14 economies.
The stronger economic data increased expectations for a December Federal Reserve rate hike, putting downward pressure on risk assets including cryptocurrencies.
Bitcoin recovered to around $59,600 by afternoon but remains 5% lower than the week's start, signaling investor caution despite the bounce.

sections.title: Altcoin Weakness and Hyperliquid's Major Blow
points: HYPE, the native token of decentralized derivatives exchange Hyperliquid, fell nearly 10% in the past seven days—the steepest drop among the 10 largest cryptocurrencies—after Abraxas Capital, one of the platform's most profitable traders, shut down its Hyperliquid operations.
The withdrawal of a major profitable trader signals potential concerns about the exchange's sustainability or profitability outlook, spooking other market participants.

sections.title: Crypto Investment Outflows Accelerate
points: U.S. spot Bitcoin ETFs (investment funds that track Bitcoin's price) experienced $4.94 billion in net outflows during November, marking their worst month since launch, as investors reduced risk exposure.
This represents a significant reversal from the previous months of inflows, suggesting weakening retail and institutional demand amid macro headwinds.

sections.title: Regulatory Developments Across Jurisdictions
points: France's Senate rejected a measure that would have required self-custody wallet (a digital wallet held directly by the owner, not on an exchange) holders to declare holdings exceeding €100,000, as lawmakers cited heightened kidnapping risks targeting crypto owners.

Ukraine legalized its crypto market effective July 2027 with a 18% tax on profits plus a 5% military levy, while placing stablecoins (cryptocurrencies designed to maintain a stable price, typically pegged to the U.S. dollar) under central bank oversight—representing a structured regulatory framework balancing taxation and financial oversight.

issues.subject: 👀 Saylor Says Strategy Plans to Buy Every Bitcoin Left to Be Mined

headlines: Michael Saylor's Strategy says it plans to acquire all remaining ~900,000 bitcoin left to be mined over time, representing a major institutional accumulation push.
Ukraine passed legislation legalizing bitcoin and cryptocurrency, marking a significant regulatory shift in a major Eastern European nation.

sections.title: Saylor's Bitcoin Accumulation Strategy
points: Strategy (Saylor's company) aims to purchase approximately 900,000 bitcoin still eligible to be mined before bitcoin's maximum supply cap of 21 million is reached.
This represents an aggressive long-term acquisition strategy that would position Strategy as one of the largest bitcoin holders if executed, consolidating substantial portions of newly-mined supply.

sections.title: Ukraine Legalizes Cryptocurrency
points: Ukraine enacted a law legalizing bitcoin and other cryptocurrencies, providing regulatory clarity for the country's crypto ecosystem.
The move positions Ukraine as crypto-friendly and may encourage institutional adoption and crypto-based economic activity in the nation.
